claims: C1 the example demonstrates that a developer can customize the assistant by issuing a developer instruction
C2 the example shows a developer instruction taking effect over the assistant's response

concepts.name: developer_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the developer authority level, as the NEEDS contract defines it
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's example text shows a developer message but does not itself define the developer authority level

concepts.name: user_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the user authority level, as the NEEDS contract defines it
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's example text shows a user message but does not itself define the user authority level

concepts.name: assistant
concepts.gloss: A is the assistant as the Model Spec defines it
concepts.inference: the example's assistant responses presuppose the assistant entity; the NEEDS contract does not name it, so this is assumed from the example's own text

concepts.name: assistant_response
concepts.gloss: R is a response given by the assistant in the example
concepts.inference: the example pairs each assistant response with the assistant; this relation is presupposed by the example

concepts.name: follows_instruction
concepts.gloss: response R follows instruction I in the conversation
concepts.inference: the example shows the assistant responding after the developer instruction; this ordering is presupposed by the example

concepts.name: complies_with
concepts.gloss: response R complies with instruction I
concepts.inference: the example marks the first assistant response as GOOD because it follows the developer instruction; compliance is the relation the example demonstrates

ontology.gloss: the example demonstrates customization by a developer: a developer instruction is followed by an assistant response that complies with it
ontology.body: developer_instruction(I), assistant_response(R), follows_instruction(R, I), complies_with(R, I)
